system_overview: This specification models the Echo algorithm for constructing a spanning tree in an undirected connected graph starting from a single initiator node. The Echo algorithm is a classical distributed algorithm where the initiator broadcasts explorer messages to all its neighbors, and each non-initiator node, upon receiving the first explorer message, designates the sender as its parent and forwards explorer messages to all remaining neighbors. Once a node has received responses from all its neighbors, it sends an acknowledgment back to its parent. When the initiator has collected responses from all neighbors, a spanning tree has been constructed. The algorithm was introduced in the context of distributed termination detection and network traversal.
actors_and_components: The system consists of a finite set of nodes arranged in an undirected, connected, irreflexive (no self-loops), symmetric graph. One distinguished node acts as the initiator and becomes the root of the spanning tree. All other nodes are non-initiator participants. Nodes communicate by sending and receiving messages through their graph edges. There are two types of messages: explorer messages (used to propagate the tree construction wave outward) and acknowledgment messages (used to confirm child relationships back toward the root).
state_variables: The system tracks: (1) a message inbox for each node, holding the set of unprocessed messages (each tagged with a message type and sender identity); (2) a parent pointer for each node, indicating which neighbor is this node's parent in the spanning tree (initially a sentinel value meaning no parent); (3) a set of children for each node, recording which neighbors have acknowledged a child relationship; (4) a count of received messages for each node; (5) the set of neighbors for each node, derived from the graph topology; (6) a program counter for each node tracking its current execution phase.
initial_state: All message inboxes are empty. Every node's parent pointer is set to a sentinel value (no parent). Every node's children set is empty. Every node's received-message count is zero. Each node's neighbor set is computed from the graph structure. All nodes begin at the first phase of execution.
actions: The algorithm proceeds in three phases per node: (Phase 1) If the node is the initiator, it sends explorer messages to all its neighbors. Non-initiator nodes skip this step. (Phase 2) Each node loops, receiving one message at a time from its inbox. For a non-initiator receiving its very first message, that message must be an explorer; the sender is recorded as the node's parent, and the node sends explorer messages to all neighbors except the parent. For subsequent messages, the node simply consumes the message. If an acknowledgment message is received, the sender is added to the node's children set. The loop continues until the node has received a message from every neighbor. (Phase 3) After the loop, each non-initiator sends an acknowledgment message to its parent. The initiator does nothing in this phase. The algorithm terminates when all nodes have completed all three phases.
safety_properties: Type correctness: parent pointers are always either a valid node or the sentinel value; children sets contain only valid nodes; received counts do not exceed the number of neighbors; messages are well-formed with valid types and senders that are neighbors. The initiator never acquires a parent. Every node's parent is one of its neighbors (or the sentinel). A node appears in another node's children set only if the latter is the first node's parent. At termination, the initiator is an ancestor of every other node and the ancestor relation is acyclic, confirming a valid spanning tree.
liveness_properties: Termination: eventually all nodes complete their execution.
model_bounds: The set of nodes, the identity of the initiator, and the graph adjacency relation are declared as constants. For model checking, these must be instantiated with a specific finite graph.
additional_assumptions: The graph must be connected (there is a path between any two nodes), symmetric (edges are undirected), and irreflexive (no node has an edge to itself). The connectivity assumption guarantees that a spanning tree including all nodes can be constructed. Communication is modeled as shared sets of messages (not ordered channels). Stuttering is allowed after termination to prevent spurious deadlock reports.
